skill.name: skill-best-practices
skill.description: Guides creation, review, validation, and troubleshooting of AI skills and SKILL.md files. Use it for frontmatter, trigger design, workflow patterns, and repository checks.
skill.summary: Create reliable AI skills with clear triggers, structured instructions, practical tests, and validation guidance.
skill.author: dboeckli

security_audit.summary: All 91 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, bounded local validation, or ordinary path handling. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found. Remote validation still has a medium supply-chain risk because it executes an unpinned npm package.

remediation.issue: Remote validation automatically executes the latest available skills package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited package version for npx, document the network action, and require explicit confirmation before remote validation.

static_findings.snippet: - Write YAML frontmatter with `name` and `description` (see Technical requirements)
Follow the recommended template: `## Instructions` → numbered steps → `## Examples` → `## Troublesho
Be specific and actionable. Move detailed docs to `references/` and link to them.
- `CLAUDE.md` — skill table under "Included Skills" (Trigger column: one-line description of when it
- `README.md` — skill table under "Enthaltene Skills" (Beschreibung column: German one-liner)
Also invoke the `cc-best-practices` skill when working on skills in this repository to ensure contex
Fix any `FAIL` lines before continuing. Common issues:
- `description` uses block scalar (`>` or `|`) → replace with a quoted single-line string
After pushing, also run the remote check to confirm `npx skills add --list` finds all skills:
- `SKILL.md` (required): Instructions in Markdown with YAML frontmatter
- `assets/` (optional): Templates, fonts, icons used in output
3. Linked files in `references/`: loaded on demand
- Folder: **kebab-case** only (`notion-project-setup`) — no spaces, underscores, or capitals
- No `README.md` inside the skill folder (put docs in `SKILL.md` or `references/`)
Structure: `[What it does] + [When to use it] + [Key capabilities]`
Run `python scripts/validate.py --input {filename}` to check data format.
**Use progressive disclosure** — keep SKILL.md focused on core instructions; move detailed docs to `
| "Could not find SKILL.md" | Wrong filename             | Rename exactly to `SKILL.md`       |
| "Invalid frontmatter"     | YAML formatting            | Add `---` delimiters, close quotes |
1. **Too verbose** — keep concise, use bullet points, move details to `references/`
2. **Instructions buried** — put critical instructions at top, use `## Critical` headers
For detailed examples and implementation templates for each pattern, consult `references/patterns.md
- [ ] `cc-best-practices` skill was loaded during this session
- [ ] After push: `validate-skills.sh --remote` run — all skills found by `npx skills`
| "Invalid frontmatter"     | YAML formatting            | Add `---` delimiters, close quotes |
| "Invalid skill name"      | Spaces or capitals in name | Use kebab-case                     |

content.value_statement: AI skills often fail because triggers, structure, and validation are unclear. This guide provides practical patterns for reliable SKILL.md design, testing, and maintenance.
actual_capabilities: Plans two or three concrete use cases before skill implementation.
Reviews skill names, descriptions, trigger phrases, and YAML frontmatter.
Provides structures for instructions, examples, troubleshooting, and linked references.
Explains progressive disclosure and five reusable workflow patterns.
Guides trigger testing, functional testing, and performance comparison.
Includes a script for local frontmatter checks and optional remote discovery checks.
limitations: Guidance targets Anthropic-style skill layouts and may not match every marketplace.
Remote validation requires Git, Node.js, npm, and network access.
Trigger rates are not measured automatically; users must run representative queries.
Repository table updates are specific to the upstream project structure.

use_cases.title: Create a New Skill
use_cases.description: Turn a workflow idea into a structured skill with clear triggers, instructions, examples, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Evaluate frontmatter, instruction quality, progressive disclosure, testing coverage, and troubleshooting guidance.

use_cases.title: Fix Trigger Behavior
use_cases.description: Refine descriptions and negative triggers when a skill loads too rarely or on unrelated requests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill plan for [goal]. Define three use cases, trigger phrases, required tools, workflow steps, and expected results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a skill from a simple workflow idea

prompt_templates.title: Write a Skill Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this skill description: [description]. Include its purpose, specific trigger phrases, important capabilities, and clear exclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a SKILL.md File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [SKILL.md content]. Report pass, warning, or fail for frontmatter, triggers, instructions, examples, references, testing, and troubleshooting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Checking an existing skill before release

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-tool skill for [workflow]. Include dependencies, validation gates, rollback steps, tool selection rules, error handling, and test cases.

output_examples.input: Create a skill that plans sprints in Linear.
output_examples.output: A three-use-case plan with sprint triggers, ordered Linear actions, validation gates, error handling, and representative tests.

output_examples.input: Review my skill because it rarely loads automatically.
output: Fail: The description does not include phrases users commonly enter.
Warning: The scope is broad and lacks negative triggers.
Fix: Add task-specific phrases, exclusions, and ten paraphrased trigger tests.

output_examples.input: Improve a large skill that consumes too much context.
output_examples.output: A concise core instruction file with detailed guidance moved into clearly linked references.

best_practices: Define concrete use cases and trigger phrases before writing instructions.
Keep core instructions concise and load detailed references only when needed.
Test relevant, paraphrased, and unrelated requests before release.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague descriptions that omit real user phrases.
Do not bury critical validation steps below long background sections.
Do not rely on prose when a deterministic validation script is available.

faq.question: What files does a basic skill require?
faq.answer: A skill needs a correctly named folder and a SKILL.md file with valid YAML frontmatter.

faq.question: How should the description be written?
faq.answer: State what the skill does, when it should load, common trigger phrases, and important exclusions.

faq.question: How can I reduce unwanted triggering?
faq.answer: Narrow the scope, add negative triggers, and test unrelated prompts that resemble the target domain.

faq.question: When should references be used?
faq.answer: Move detailed examples, domain rules, and long documentation into references when they are not always required.

faq.question: Does the validator test skill quality?
faq.answer: No. It checks frontmatter and optional remote discovery, while functional quality requires representative task testing.

faq.question: Is remote validation fully offline?
faq.answer: No. Remote mode uses npm tooling and the repository URL, so it requires network access and external package execution.
